newsitem.title: USA: IBM Vermont plant to reopen after bomb threat.
newsitem.headline: IBM Vermont plant to reopen after bomb threat.

text.p: Police searched an IBM Corp semiconductor manufacturing plant after receiving a bomb threat but found nothing, the company said, adding the plant would resume operations late Wednesday.

"After a thorough investigation of the site, we have people on hand working right now to reopen the facility," IBM spokesman Tom Beermann told Reuters. "Employees who are scheduled for the second shift at 1900 EST are being asked to return to work as normal."

The Essex Junction plant, located just outside of Burlington, closed around 1700 EST Tuesday after a man told police a bomb would explode at a specific time. The plant is IBM's largest chip-manufacturing plant and, with as many as 7,000 workers, is Vermont's largest private employer.

It operates 24 hours a day, seven days a week and manufactures microprocessors which run personal computers, logic computer chips used in everything from cars to home appliances, and other semiconductor products.

Beermann said it is difficult to assess how much the production shutdown, which lasted around 25 hours, cost IBM. The Federal Bureau of Investigation was analyzing a tape of the phone call and police were pursuing leads, Essex Junction Police Lieutenant Gary Taylor said.
Bomb-sniffing dogs from Vermont and Connecticut and bomb disposal units searched the premises Tuesday and Wednesday, he said.
Beermann said IBM was cooperating with the investigation but declined to give further details.
